notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Speed signs read "Speed Limit" and use miles per hour; values ending in 5 are common.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Signs use many words: railway crossings spell out the warning, and yellow diamonds carry text. The northern neighbour uses symbols.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: The yield sign is an inverted triangle with the word "YIELD" inside; the northern neighbour leaves out the word.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: A yellow triangular "No Passing Zone" sign exists only here.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Rectangular junction warning signs with a single or double arrow, where the northern neighbour uses diamonds.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: One-way signs always carry the words "ONE WAY".

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Big green highway signs with rounded corners and white text; the northern neighbour has square corners.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: White and orange fibre optic cable markers are almost unique to this country.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow centre lines with white edge lines; double yellow centre lines are the most common.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Highways have rumble strips along the edges, and between lanes on multi-lane roads; much rarer in the north neighbour.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Small manufactured or trailer homes are popular in rural areas, especially in the Southeast.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Baptist churches are everywhere, mostly in the Southern Plains and Southeast.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Short plates with a unique design in every state; around half the states skip front plates.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 2 coverage is rare, except in Alaska, Hawaii and a few deep-South spots; Generation 3 is also scarcer than up north.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Wooden poles carry big metal cylinder transformers, and insulators sit raised on top. Typical of the northern part of the Americas, never Europe.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Post-mounted mailboxes with a small side flag are typical of North and Central America.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: At big intersections traffic lights hang from long metal mast arms, often with street signs attached.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Semi-trucks have a long nose, unlike the flat-fronted cabover trucks of Europe and Asia.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Great Plains: flat, mostly treeless farmland or dry grass from the northern border to central Texas.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Low forested mountains of beech and oak run through the east.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Red or yellow-red soil is widespread in the Deep South, from Oklahoma to South Carolina.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Red mesas and tablelands around the Four Corners.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Temperate rainforest with ferns and huge conifers on the coasts of the Pacific Northwest.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Tall branched saguaro cacti mark southern Arizona near the Mexican border.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A single-lane highway over tropical islands with sandy white soil.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Grainy "salt and pepper" road surface is typical of Texas.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow centre lines with a noticeably large gap are most common in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Oregon.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: A black stripe between the two yellow centre lines shows up in California.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poles in most of California have three yellow stripes at the base.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: White metal plates with an orange rectangle and diamond appear on most poles in Wisconsin and Michigan's Upper Peninsula.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: A thin stick with a vertical white reflector outlined in black.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Black paddle-shaped bollards are common in Utah and Wyoming, and also found in Nebraska.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Bollards with three round reflectors are common in New Mexico.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Plain white bollards with black reflectors are unique to Wisconsin.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: The usual bollard has a very long rectangular reflector on top.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Oregon speed signs often say just "Speed".

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Yellow or red bands wrap signposts in Texas.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Coastal New England houses have shingle walls and stone walls line rural roads.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Narrow one-storey wooden shotgun houses are common in New Orleans, Houston, Louisville and Mississippi.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Rounded sand-brown adobe-style Pueblo Revival houses with flat roofs are common in New Mexico.
